title: Activation tethering and fallback play notes
content:
Purpose:
Short: capture a pragmatic, cross-functional pattern for tethering activation windows across services (API, routing, cache layers) and a minimal fallback choreography that non-engineering stakeholders can read and act on. This is a scratchpad: lots of assumptions listed below.

Context and motivation:
- We keep hitting a gap where a product rollout flips a feature flag but downstream routers or dedicated capacity pools lag; users see partial behavior and support pages light up.
- Tethering = making the activation step for feature X atomic-ish across dependent surfaces (console, router, dedicated pools, telemetry). Not a true distributed transaction but a deterministic sequence + guards + quick fallback.
- Focused on canary/A-B scenarios where partial traffic and quick rollback are required.

High-level pattern (one-liner):
- Pre-stage configs -> dry-run + shadow traffic -> warm caches + pool sync -> soft-activation to microcohort -> observe signals for X minutes -> either escalate exposure or trigger automated fallback.

Stakeholders (who must be looped in):
- Product: Aisha (owner) — decides exposure cohorts
- Infra/Platform: Evan — routing/pool sync ops
- Serving runtime: Carlos — model variants & kv-cache warmup
- SRE: Priya — monitors and executes runbook rollback if manual needed
- CS/Support: rotated on-call — send templated comms

Signal ownership matrix (working, not exhaustive):
- 5xx spike (api layer): infra (Evan)
- mean latency p50/p95 increase: serving runtime (Carlos)
- quality regressions (BLEU/ROUGE/QA evals): product & applied-ml
- cost burst beyond budget: finance alert -> product + infra

Operational checklist (pre-activation, quick items):
- [ ] Feature flag entry created in FF system with GUID and annotation (who/why)
- [ ] Canary cohort definition committed in console UI + experiment id
- [ ] Routing rules for microcohort (slice ID) reviewed by Evan
- [ ] Dedicated pool scale-up tickets created and capacity reserved (if Dedicated mode)
- [ ] KV-cache warmup plan for model variants (list of prefixes to preheat)
- [ ] Runbook stub (this doc) linked from the ticket and assigned
- [ ] Stakeholder comms scheduled (pre, during, post windows)

Activation timeline (typical small-scale run):
- T-minus 45m: confirm pool/capacity and dry-run in staging shadow traffic (no exposure)
- T-minus 20m: start cache warmup for variant V2 using shadow replay (target 95% hit)
- T-minus 10m: open observability windows and ensure dashboards pre-populated with baselines
- 0m: flip soft flag -> 0.5% microcohort (slice A)
- +10m: evaluate short-term signals (latency, errors, basic quality smoke tests)
- +30m: widen to 5% if signals nominal; otherwise fallback immediately
- +2h: decision point to move to 20% or rollback

Fallback choreography (automated + manual paths):
- Primary automated rule: if p95 latency > baseline*2 for 2 consecutive 5m windows OR 5xxs > 0.5% absolute increase -> automated revert flag flip and traffic re-route to baseline model (priority: restore availability over quality)
- Secondary manual reversion: SRE to run quick revert play earlier if complex failure that automation doesn't catch (e.g., soft degradation of ranking quality)
- Triage kickoff: once reverted, product + applied-ml to pull sample requests and label urgent regressions

Guardrails and safety heuristics (practical thresholds):
- Do not exceed 20% exposure without an explicit executive signoff (unless experiment type is low-risk A/B)
- Stop widening if cost per 1k tokens increases > 30% for a sustained 30m window
- Never warm up variants that are not in the model catalog without an approval note (safety/compliance)

Telemetry and dashboards to populate before launch (minimal set):
- API: request rate, 4xx/5xx counts, p50/p95 latency by slice
- Serving runtime: oks per model variant, queue depth, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate
- Quality: run the smoke prompts set (10 canonical prompts) and track top-1 regression differences
- Cost: per-slice cost burn rate (tokens * pricing) and dedicated GPU minutes used

Comms templates (copyable snippets):
- Pre-launch announcement (to SRE/infra/support): "Planned soft activation for EXP-1123 at 14:00 PT. Slice A = 0.5%; watch p95 latency, 5xx rate. Owner: Aisha. If automated revert occurs, SRE will post summary."
- Post-rollback summary (to execs): include timestamp, trigger metric, immediate user impact estimate, next steps

Open questions / risks to resolve (TODOs):
- How do we automatically verify cross-surface sync of route and pool? (Health check ping on every node?)
- Should we add a token-budget-based auto-throttle to avoid runaway cost during a canary?
- Minimal contract for canary samples: n >= 500 requests or 30m running time (which is better?)

Runbook snippets (commands / quick references):
- Revert flag via FF console: FF_URL/flags/EXP-1123 -> set to baseline -> confirm via API: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/flags/EXP-1123
- Force-routing to baseline (infra): POST /routing/override {slice: "A", target: "baseline"} (requires infra-ops token)
- Cache flush + warmup (serving): ./scripts/kv_warmup.sh --model v2 --prefixes file://warmup-list.txt

Engineering notes (to Carlos/Evan):
- Consider adding a lightweight two-phase activation: 1) config push to nodes (no traffic), 2) route flip. This reduces mid-window drift when nodes pull configs at different times.
- Investigate exposing a simple "activation state" endpoint that returns {config_commit, active_variant, ready_ok} to drive the final commit decision from the console.

Post-mortem checklist (if rollback):
- Capture 5k sample requests from the canary slice and store in dedicated S3 prefix
- Run automated diff against baseline on the smoke prompt set + 50 random user samples
- Convene 1-hour war-room with product + SRE + applied-ml within 4 hours of rollback

Action items (next 7 days):
- [ ] Evan: prototype a route-health endpoint that reports commit sync across nodes (ETA 1w)
- [ ] Carlos: draft a kv-warmup checklist and automation script (ETA 3d)
- [ ] Aisha: finalize microcohort list for the next canary (ETA 2d)
- [ ] Priya: update oncall runbook with automated revert thresholds (ETA 4d)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the early splits tiny. Humans forget that a 1% split can still be thousands of requests for high-volume customers.
- Support needs bullet-pointed lines to copy into Zendesk — make a small template.

References / reading:
- quick ideas from previous canary that tripped routing: INF-800 (postmortem)
- internal appendix: rollout-safety-heuristics (confluence link above)

Version history:
- 2024-11-20: initial notes and pattern sketch (Aisha)
- 2024-12-05: added signal matrix and activation timeline (Evan)
- 2025-02-10: refined automated fallback thresholds and action items (Aisha)

---
If you see something missing or an obvious short-circuit (we can make this less ceremony-heavy), flag it inline and I'll tidy before converting to playbook template.
